description.en-US: The order this line belongs to. Immutable: moving a line between orders would change two orders' totals at once, and the one it left would keep a total it can no longer justify.
Display order within the order. It matters more here than on most documents because section and note lines organize the ones around them, and a reordered list would regroup them.

Whether this line buys something or merely organizes the document. Only a product line carries a quantity and a price and contributes to the totals; section, subsection and note lines are layout. The fields a product line requires are enforced by the domain service rather than by required_for_create, because the schema cannot express a requirement conditional on another field.

What is being bought. The variant, not the template: the variant is the transactable unit, while whether it may be purchased at all is a flag on its parent template. A plain ulid, since the product belongs to Inventory. Required for a product line, absent on the others.
What appears on the printed order. For a section or note line this is the whole content of the line.
How much is being ordered, expressed in uom_id. This value and its unit are what the buyer chose, and neither is ever overwritten by a conversion (BR-UOM-PUR-004).

The unit the buyer is ordering in, which need not be the unit stock is counted in: a case of twelve is bought by the case and stocked by the unit. It must share a category with the product's inventory unit, which is checked through Essential's conversion port (BR-UOM-PUR-001, 009).

The same quantity converted into the product's inventory unit, so that a receipt does not have to re-derive it. Computed, never accepted from a client: a supplied value could disagree with the conversion and would then be believed by whatever books the goods in (BR-UOM-PUR-003).
Price per unit of uom_id, in the order's currency. Defaulted from the agreement line when the order draws against one.

Which vendor price quote this line's price was resolved from, when one applied. A plain ulid and NOT a foreign key: the reference records where the number came from, and a quote that is later archived or deleted must not take the order line with it. Empty means no vendor price applied and the price was typed by hand (section 29). Never written back to: overriding the line changes this order and nothing else (TS-PRICE-07).

What the vendor price resolution returned, before any human changed it. Kept beside unit_price rather than replacing it so that an override is visible as the difference between the two — a line quoted at 9,500 and negotiated to 9,200 shows both numbers, where storing only the agreed one would lose the fact that a negotiation happened. Empty when no vendor price applied; equal to unit_price when the resolved price was accepted unchanged.
A percentage off this line, bounded at 100 because a discount that exceeds the price would make the vendor pay the buyer.
When this particular line is expected, which may differ from the order's date when one item is back-ordered.
Quantity times unit price, less the discount, before tax. Stored rather than computed on read so that the order's totals are a plain sum; recomputed by the domain service on every line write.

The tax on this line. Deliberately an input, not a calculation: there is no tax engine and the requirement forbids building one here, so the client states the tax and the server sums it. This is the one amount on a line that is not no_update.
